questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That the destination was within Central or South America. Also the subjects’ relevance to my studies.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think it was a bit difficult. The university itself did not do much for the exchange student community in my opinion.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had three orientation days as exchange students prior to the semester start.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy, I arranged it through WhatsApp. Other KU students had recommended this housing on a Facebook group for students going to Latin America.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It was a bit harder to participate in on campus activities at night, since it wasn’t that safe to go outside at night.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There were two portals and some things you could only register in one of them. The portals would close down every few minutes, so it was difficult to research the courses, also because there weren’t any descriptions of the courses in the portals.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A contact person in the exchange department on campus, who you could also contact through teams.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Somewhat successful. Except for the fact that I couldn’t change one of the courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Research it thoroughly beforehand. But it is a bit difficult to do on their website.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The whole system is quite different to KU. There were a lot more smaller tests and a lot of group work. I would say the level is lower.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot more interactive teaching through tests, projects, group work etc.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Música en America latina
Los animales en la historia 
Contextos de America latina y Colombia 
Arqueología de Colombia
Arte en Colombia 
Art and travel

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them, except contextos de America latina y Colombia, because I think it was a bit too difficult to follow in Spanish, unless you speak and understand it perfectly. The other subjects were very interesting and easier to follow.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None really

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were more expensive than I expected. Rent was also a bit higher than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Sports were of high quality! There was an amazing sports center on campus with several gyms, a huge swimming pool and classes (yoga, dance, pilates, badminton, chess etc.). But the clubs I signed up for only had an event once.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You could go to sports classes of all sorts, and there were Japanese clubs, cultural exchange club, volunteering for animals club etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The sports and dance classes. They were great!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel the country, especially to the Caribbean coast of Colombia.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: At first it was very difficult but once you made friends it was much better.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Living off campus so you’re forced to speak Spanish with local students. On campus housing was mostly exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Punctuality was very different (it was normal to be late).

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The way they value social life very highly, and how easy it is to become part of a big friend group. Their dance culture is very rich too. They are also very helpful.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: To make sure to show up and socialize on the intro days. To travel a lot while you can and also research a lot on the university’s website beforehand.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: That you can’t switch your courses once you’ve chosen them. Also that the university only arrange one thing for exchange students, so don’t rely on them to create a space for the exchange community - it can get very lonely.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting a group of amazing Colombian friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being very lonely and feeling that it was impossible to meet people and make friends. Also feeling unsafe and being robbed.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
